- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.3–0.7) and forecast shows strong trend continuation, apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid over-leveraging momentum.  
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, re-weight forecast toward recent 7-day average to reduce horizon bias.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
